D iplomats, captains of industry and prominent Nigerians gathered in Lagos to celebrate the 78th birthday of the British monarch, King Charles III, and the longstanding relationship between the United Kingdom and Nigeria.
The celebration, held at the residence of the British Deputy High Commissioner in Ikoyi, Lagos, was hosted by the British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Pete Vowles, and the Deputy High Commissioner, Jonny Baxter.
Among the dignitaries at the event were the Yeye Oodua, Erelu Dr Abiola Dosunmu; Senior Pastor of House on the Rock, Pastor Paul Adefarasin; Lagos State Secretary to the State Government, Bimbola Salu-Hundeyin; and founder and Chief Executive Officer of EbonyLife Group, Mo Abudu.
Others included the founder and president of the Wellbeing Foundation Africa, Toyin Saraki, as well as members of the diplomatic community, business leaders and other distinguished guests.
The evening also featured musical performances by the Shuga Life Band, while cocktails and wines added to the festivities.
The gathering provided an opportunity to celebrate the longstanding friendship between the UK and Nigeria, as well as their shared interests and partnerships across various sectors.
